title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 16. The Manifestation of All Energies
html:
The play in Chandrashekhara's house continues: Haridasa, Advaita and Nityananda enter; the Lord appears as a gopi, then in the mood of Kamala and of the Goddess, displays all power, feeds the devotees with milk and in the morning returns home

Verse 1

प्राविशत्तदनु दण्डधरोऽग्रतः
पूर्णचन्द्रसदृशो हरिदासः।
कीर्तनं कुरु हरेरिति वादी
बोधयंस्त्रिजगतीं परितप्ताम्॥१॥

prāviśattadanu daṇḍadharo'grataḥ
pūrṇacandrasadṛśo haridāsaḥ|
kīrtanaṁ kuru hareriti vādī
bodhayaṁstrijagatīṁ paritaptām||1||

pravishat — entered; tat-anu — then; danda-dharah — bearing a staff; agratah — first; purna-chandra-sadrishah — like the full moon; haridasah — Haridasa; kirtanam — kirtana; kuru — perform; hareh — of Hari; iti — thus; vadi — saying; bodhayan — awakening; tri-jagatim — the three worlds; paritaptam — burning (with suffering).

1Then Haridasa, like the full moon, entered first, a staff in his hand1. "Sing the kirtana of Hari!" he proclaimed, awakening the three worlds, which burn with suffering.

Verse 2

तस्य तद्वचनमब्जमुखस्य
सन्निपीय हृषिताङ्गरुहास्ते।
वैष्णवा ननृतुरुद्गतनेत्र-
वारिभिस्तिमितविग्रहभाजः॥२॥

tasya tadvacanamabjamukhasya
sannipīya hṛṣitāṅgaruhāste|
vaiṣṇavā nanṛturudgatanetra-
vāribhistimitavigrahabhājaḥ||2||

tasya — his; tat — those; vachanam — words; abja-mukhasya — of the lotus-faced one; sannipiya — drinking in; hrishita-anga-ruhah — their hair bristling with joy; te — those; vaishnavah — Vaishnavas; nanrituh — danced; udgata-netra-varibhih — with tears welling from their eyes; stimita-vigraha-bhajah — their bodies drenched.

2Drinking in those words of the lotus-faced Haridasa, the Vaishnavas danced; their hair bristled with joy, and their bodies were drenched with the tears that welled from their eyes.

Verse 3

प्राविशत्तदनु वैष्णवराजो
राजमान इव तिग्ममरीचिः।
आक्षिपन्निव सुधामिव कान्ति-
मब्जचारुवदनः स महात्मा॥३॥

prāviśattadanu vaiṣṇavarājo
rājamāna iva tigmamarīciḥ|
ākṣipanniva sudhāmiva kānti-
mabjacāruvadanaḥ sa mahātmā||3||

pravishat — entered; tat-anu — then; vaishnava-rajah — the king of Vaishnavas; rajamanah — shining; iva — like; tigma-marichih — the fierce-rayed sun; akshipan — scattering; iva — as if; sudham — nectar; iva — like; kantim — radiance; abja-charu-vadanah — his face lovely as a lotus; sah — that; maha-atma — great soul.

3Then the king of the Vaishnavas entered, shining like the fierce-rayed sun, as though scattering a radiance like nectar all around — the great soul whose face was lovely as a lotus.

Verse 4

ईश्वरस्य कलया तु विजातो-
ऽद्वैतवर्य इतरैरनुगैः सः।
आननर्त हरिपादरसार्द्रो
मत्तसिंह इव दुर्दमनान्तः॥४॥

īśvarasya kalayā tu vijāto-
'dvaitavarya itarairanugaiḥ saḥ|
ānanarta haripādarasārdro
mattasiṁha iva durdamanāntaḥ||4||

ishvarasya — of the Lord; kalaya — from a portion; tu — indeed; vijatah — born; advaita-varyah — the excellent Advaita; itaraih — with the other; anugaih — followers; sah — he; ananarta — danced; hari-pada-rasa-ardrah — moist with the rasa of Hari's feet; matta-simhah — a maddened lion; iva — like; durdamana-antah — untamable within.

4The excellent Advaita, born of a portion of the Lord2, moist with the rasa of Hari's feet, danced together with the other followers like a maddened lion, untamable within.

Verse 5

तं विलोक्य मुदितैर्नयनाब्जैः
साधवः सदसि तस्य मुखेन्दुम्।
अद्भुतं पपुरवश्यहृदस्ते
प्रेमसागररसेषु निमग्नाः॥५॥

taṁ vilokya muditairnayanābjaiḥ
sādhavaḥ sadasi tasya mukhendum|
adbhutaṁ papuravaśyahṛdaste
premasāgararaseṣu nimagnāḥ||5||

tam — him; vilokya — seeing; muditaih — joyful; nayana-abjaih — with lotus eyes; sadhavah — the saintly; sadasi — in the assembly; tasya — his; mukha-indum — moon-face; adbhutam — wondrous; papuh — drank; avashya-hridah — their hearts overpowered; te — they; prema-sagara-raseshu — in the rasas of the ocean of love; nimagnah — immersed.

5The saintly ones in the assembly, gazing at Him with joyful lotus eyes, drank in the wondrous moon of His face; their hearts were overpowered, and they sank into the rasas of the ocean of love.

Verse 6

गोपीवेशधरको बलदेवः
प्राविशद्रसविशेषविनोदी।
प्राणनाथकरपल्लवप्रधृतो
नयनवारिपरिपूर्णस्वदेहः॥६॥

gopīveśadharako baladevaḥ
prāviśadrasaviśeṣavinodī|
prāṇanāthakarapallavapradhṛto
nayanavāriparipūrṇasvadehaḥ||6||

gopi-vesha-dharakah — wearing the dress of a gopi; baladevah — Baladeva; pravishat — entered; rasa-vishesha-vinodi — delighting in a special rasa; prana-natha-kara-pallava-pradhritah — holding (or held by) the bud-like hand of the Lord of his life; nayana-vari-paripurna-sva-dehah — his body flooded with tears.

6Baladeva3 too entered, in the dress of a gopi, delighting in a special rasa; He held the bud-like hand of the Lord of His life, and His whole body was flooded with tears.

Verse 7

वासुदेवकृतवेशविशेषः
प्राविशत्स भगवानमृतांशुः।
तप्तकाञ्चनवपुः कनकाद्रि-
शृङ्गराज इव जङ्गमवेशः॥७॥

vāsudevakṛtaveśaviśeṣaḥ
prāviśatsa bhagavānamṛtāṁśuḥ|
taptakāñcanavapuḥ kanakādri-
śṛṅgarāja iva jaṅgamaveśaḥ||7||

vasudeva-krita-vesha-visheshah — Vasudeva, having put on a special attire; pravishat — entered; sah — He; bhagavan — Bhagavan; amrita-amshuh — the moon; tapta-kanchana-vapuh — His body like molten gold; kanaka-adri-shringa-rajah — the king of the peaks of the golden mountain; iva — like; jangama-veshah — in moving form.

7And Bhagavan Himself entered, Vasudeva in a special attire4, like the moon; His body was the colour of molten gold, and He was like the king of the peaks of the golden mountain set in motion.

Verse 8

गोपिकेव वरकञ्चुलिवक्षाः
शङ्खकङ्कणधरोऽरुणवस्त्रः।
नूपुरेण नुतपादसुपद्मः
सूक्ष्ममध्यवपुषा स ननर्त॥८॥

gopikeva varakañculivakṣāḥ
śaṅkhakaṅkaṇadharo'ruṇavastraḥ|
nūpureṇa nutapādasupadmaḥ
sūkṣmamadhyavapuṣā sa nanarta||8||

gopika — a gopi; iva — like; vara-kanchuli-vakshah — with a fine bodice on His breast; shankha-kankana-dharah — wearing conch-shell bangles; aruna-vastrah — in red garments; nupurena — by an anklet; nuta-pada-su-padmah — His fine lotus feet praised (by its tinkling); sukshma-madhya-vapusha — with a slender waist; sah — He; nanarta — danced.

8Like a gopi, with a fine bodice on His breast, wearing conch-shell bangles and red garments, His lotus feet praised by the tinkling of His anklets, He danced, slender-waisted and lithe.

Verse 9

ज्योतिषातिमिरिते भुवस्तले
देहजेन नृहरेः कृते तदा।
दिव्यगन्धपवनः स कम्पयन्
मालतीं मलयजो ववौ मुहुः॥९॥

jyotiṣātimirite bhuvastale
dehajena nṛhareḥ kṛte tadā|
divyagandhapavanaḥ sa kampayan
mālatīṁ malayajo vavau muhuḥ||9||

jyotisha — by the light; atimirite — freed of darkness; bhuvah — of the earth; tale — (when) the surface; deha-jena — born of the body; nrihareh — of Nrihari; krite — was made; tada — then; divya-gandha-pavanah — the divinely fragrant breeze; sah — that; kampayan — stirring; malatim — the malati jasmine; malaya-jah — born on Malaya; vavau — blew; muhuh — again and again.

9When the light that shone from Nrihari's body had driven the darkness from the face of the earth, the breeze from Malaya5, laden with divine fragrance, blew again and again, stirring the malati jasmine.

Verse 10

खेदशोककलया विदितोऽपि
पूर्णमण्डल इव प्रचकाशे।
चन्द्रमा दिवि सुरेशमहेश-
लोकपालसगणावृतमार्गे॥१०॥

khedaśokakalayā vidito'pi
pūrṇamaṇḍala iva pracakāśe|
candramā divi sureśamaheśa-
lokapālasagaṇāvṛtamārge||10||

kheda-shoka-kalaya — by its digit of distress and sorrow (its waning); viditah — known; api — though; purna-mandalah — a full disc; iva — like; prachakashe — shone; chandrama — the moon; divi — in the sky; sura-isha-maha-isha-loka-pala-sa-gana-avrita-marge — on a path thronged by the lord of the gods, Mahesha and the guardians of the worlds with their hosts.

10And the moon, though known for the waning that brings distress and sorrow, shone in the sky as if full-orbed, on a path thronged by the lord of the gods, Mahesha and the guardians of the worlds with their hosts.

Verse 11

कीर्तनं स भगवानतितेजा
नर्तनं च मुदितः प्रचकार।
भावमाशु विदधे कमलायाः
कान्तिभावभृद्वपुषोऽस्याः॥११॥

kīrtanaṁ sa bhagavānatitejā
nartanaṁ ca muditaḥ pracakāra|
bhāvamāśu vidadhe kamalāyāḥ
kāntibhāvabhṛdvapuṣo'syāḥ||11||

kirtanam — kirtana; sah — He; bhagavan — Bhagavan; ati-tejah — of surpassing splendour; nartanam — dance; cha — and; muditah — joyful; prachakara — performed; bhavam — the mood; ashu — at once; vidadhe — assumed; kamalayah — of Kamala; kanti-bhava-bhrit-vapushah — His body bearing (her) beauty and feeling; asyah — her.

11Bhagavan, of surpassing splendour, joyfully led the kirtana and the dance, and soon He assumed the mood of Kamala6 — His body took on her beauty and her feeling.

Verse 12

तत्र देवगृहमध्यगतायाः
कृष्णदिव्यवपुषः प्रतिमायाः।
सन्निकर्षमुपसृत्य विनीतो
नव्यवस्त्रदशया कुसुमानि॥१२॥

tatra devagṛhamadhyagatāyāḥ
kṛṣṇadivyavapuṣaḥ pratimāyāḥ|
sannikarṣamupasṛtya vinīto
navyavastradaśayā kusumāni||12||

tatra — there; deva-griha-madhya-gatayah — standing in the middle of the shrine; krishna-divya-vapushah — of Krishna's divine form; pratimayah — of the Deity; sannikarsham — near; upasritya — approaching; vinitah — humbly; navya-vastra-dashaya — with the fringe of a new cloth; kusumani — the flowers.

12There, in the middle of the shrine, stood the Deity of Krishna in His divine form. Humbly approaching it, with the fringe of a new cloth

Verse 13

विग्रहादपनयन्पुनरेव
तत्र तानि निदधे सुमनांसि।
प्रेमभक्तिरसपूरितकोटि-
मातृस्नेहपरिपूरितोऽभवत्॥१३॥

vigrahādapanayanpunareva
tatra tāni nidadhe sumanāṁsi|
premabhaktirasapūritakoṭi-
mātṛsnehaparipūrito'bhavat||13||

vigrahat — from the Deity; apanayan — removing; punah eva — once again; tatra — there; tani — those; nidadhe — placed; sumanamsi — flowers; prema-bhakti-rasa-purita-koti-matri-sneha-paripuritah — filled with the affection of millions of mothers, full of the rasa of loving devotion; abhavat — became.

13He took the flowers off the Deity and placed them there again — and was filled with the affection of millions of mothers, full of the rasa of loving devotion.

Verse 14

तां स्त्रियं प्रमुदिताः परिनेमुः
संस्तवेन श्रुतिभिः प्रतुष्टुवुः।
आज्ञया सकलदेवमयस्य
तस्य हृष्टमनसो द्विजमुख्याः॥१४॥

tāṁ striyaṁ pramuditāḥ parinemuḥ
saṁstavena śrutibhiḥ pratuṣṭuvuḥ|
ājñayā sakaladevamayasya
tasya hṛṣṭamanaso dvijamukhyāḥ||14||

tam — to that; striyam — woman; pramuditah — rejoicing; parinemuh — bowed down; samstavena — with praise; shrutibhih — with Vedic verses; pratushtuvuh — glorified; ajnaya — by the command; sakala-deva-mayasya — of Him who comprises all the gods; tasya — His; hrishta-manasah — glad at heart; dvija-mukhyah — the foremost brahmanas.

14At the command of Him who comprises all the gods, the foremost brahmanas, rejoicing and glad at heart, bowed down to that woman and glorified her with hymns of praise and verses of the Vedas.

Verse 15

तत्क्षणात्पुनरभूद्भगवत्याः
सर्वशक्तिमयतां तु वहन्त्याः।
भाव एव सुजना मुदमापु-
स्तुष्टुवुः सुरकृतैः स्तवराजैः॥१५॥

tatkṣaṇātpunarabhūdbhagavatyāḥ
sarvaśaktimayatāṁ tu vahantyāḥ|
bhāva eva sujanā mudamāpu-
stuṣṭuvuḥ surakṛtaiḥ stavarājaiḥ||15||

tat-kshanat — at that moment; punah — again; abhut — arose; bhagavatyah — of the Goddess; sarva-shakti-mayatam — all-powerfulness; tu — indeed; vahantyah — bearing; bhavah — the mood; eva — itself; su-janah — the good people; mudam — joy; apuh — attained; tushtuvuh — praised; sura-kritaih — composed by the gods; stava-rajaih — with royal hymns.

15And at that very moment there arose in Him again the mood of the Goddess Herself, who bears all power7; the good people were filled with joy and praised Her with royal hymns composed by the gods.

Verse 16

आसने समुपविश्य सुक्लृप्ते
देवताप्रतिकृती पुनराह।
प्राविशं नटनवीक्षणकामा-
ऽत्रागतास्मि भवतां कुतुकेन॥१६॥

āsane samupaviśya suklṛpte
devatāpratikṛtī punarāha|
prāviśaṁ naṭanavīkṣaṇakāmā-
'trāgatāsmi bhavatāṁ kutukena||16||

asane — on a seat; samupavishya — sitting down; su-klipte — beautifully arranged; devata-pratikriti — the likeness of the Goddess; punah — again; aha — said; pravisham — I entered; natana-vikshana-kama — wishing to watch the dancing; atra — here; agata asmi — I have come; bhavatam — your; kutukena — out of curiosity.

16Seated on a beautifully arranged seat, that likeness of the Goddess spoke again: "I have come in here wishing to watch your dancing — I came out of curiosity."

Verse 17

देहि देवि तव पादयुगाब्जे
प्रेमभक्तिमिति ते पुनरूचुः।
अब्रवीच्च मयि ते यदि भक्ति-
र्जायते यदि वदिष्यति लोकः॥१७॥

dehi devi tava pādayugābje
premabhaktimiti te punarūcuḥ|
abravīcca mayi te yadi bhakti-
rjāyate yadi vadiṣyati lokaḥ||17||

dehi — grant; devi — O Goddess; tava — to Your; pada-yuga-abje — two lotus feet; prema-bhaktim — loving devotion; iti — thus; te — they; punah — in reply; uchuh — said; abravit — said; cha — and; mayi — to Me; te — your; yadi — if; bhaktih — devotion; jayate — arises; yadi — then; vadishyati — will say; lokah — people.

17"O Goddess, grant us loving devotion to Your lotus feet," they replied. And She said: "If devotion to Me arises in you, people will say:

Verse 18

चाण्ड एष इति सुस्मितवक्त्रा
तानुवाच तर्हि ते भुवि नेमुः।
ब्राह्मणास्तमनु सा हरिदास-
मर्क इन्दुसदृशं समग्रहीत्॥१८॥

cāṇḍa eṣa iti susmitavaktrā
tānuvāca tarhi te bhuvi nemuḥ|
brāhmaṇāstamanu sā haridāsa-
marka indusadṛśaṁ samagrahīt||18||

chandah — a votary of Chandi; eshah — this one; iti — thus; su-smita-vaktra — with a smiling face; tan — to them; uvacha — said; tarhi — then; te — those; bhuvi — to the ground; nemuh — bowed; brahmanah — brahmanas; tam anu — after that; sa — she; haridasam — Haridasa; arkah — the sun; indu-sadrisham — like the moon; samagrahit — took up (embraced).

18'This one is a votary of Chandi.'"8 So She said to them with a smile. Then the brahmanas bowed to Her to the ground, and She, like the sun, embraced Haridasa, who was like the moon.

Verse 19

पञ्चहायन इवाभवत्तदा
सोऽपि तत्र तदभूदतिचित्रम्।
तत्र कोऽपि समुवाच मुरारिं
दीनमेनमवलोकय देवि॥१९॥

pañcahāyana ivābhavattadā
so'pi tatra tadabhūdaticitram|
tatra ko'pi samuvāca murāriṁ
dīnamenamavalokaya devi||19||

pancha-hayanah — a five-year-old (child); iva — like; abhavat — became; tada — then; sah — he; api — too; tatra — there; tat — that; abhut — was; ati-chitram — most wondrous; tatra — there; ko 'pi — someone; samuvacha — said; murarim — Murari; dinam — lowly; enam — this; avalokaya — look upon; devi — O Goddess.

19And he became then like a child of five — a most wondrous sight. Someone there said: "O Goddess, look upon this lowly Murari!"

Verse 20

तन्निशम्य नयनाब्जयुगेन
प्रेमतोयमसृजत्करुणार्द्रा।
तत्क्षणात्समनुभूय च सा त-
त्पूजनं निजजनस्य सुवेशा॥२०॥

tanniśamya nayanābjayugena
prematoyamasṛjatkaruṇārdrā|
tatkṣaṇātsamanubhūya ca sā ta-
tpūjanaṁ nijajanasya suveśā||20||

tat — that; nishamya — hearing; nayana-abja-yugena — from her two lotus eyes; prema-toyam — the water of love (tears); asrijat — shed; karuna-ardra — melted with compassion; tat-kshanat — at once; samanubhuya — accepting; cha — and; sa — she; tat — that; pujanam — worship; nija-janasya — of her own people; su-vesha — beautifully attired.

20Hearing this, She, melting with compassion, shed tears of love from Her two lotus eyes; and at once, accepting the worship of Her own, beautifully attired,

Verse 21

स्तन्यमाशु विदधे सुरवर्या-
न्पाययन्नसुरवाहिनीरिपुः।
तां विलोक्य करुणार्द्रसुनेत्रा-
मीश्वरं निजजना मुदमापुः॥२१॥

stanyamāśu vidadhe suravaryā-
npāyayannasuravāhinīripuḥ|
tāṁ vilokya karuṇārdrasunetrā-
mīśvaraṁ nijajanā mudamāpuḥ||21||

stanyam — breast-milk; ashu — at once; vidadhe — produced; sura-varyan — the best of the gods; payayan — giving to drink; asura-vahini-ripuh — the Foe of the asura hosts; tam — her; vilokya — seeing; karuna-ardra-su-netram — with lovely eyes moist with compassion; ishvaram — the Lord; nija-janah — His own people; mudam — joy; apuh — attained.

21He — the Foe of the asura hosts — brought forth breast-milk and gave it to the best of the gods to drink. Seeing the Lord, His lovely eyes moist with compassion, His own people were filled with joy.

Verse 22

तत्क्षणाद्भगवतः पुनरेव
भाव ईशितुरभूदवलोक्य।
नेमुरार्द्रनयना जगदीशं
तुष्टुवुश्च मुदिता द्विजवर्याः॥२२॥

tatkṣaṇādbhagavataḥ punareva
bhāva īśiturabhūdavalokya|
nemurārdranayanā jagadīśaṁ
tuṣṭuvuśca muditā dvijavaryāḥ||22||

tat-kshanat — at once; bhagavatah — in Bhagavan; punah eva — once more; bhavah — the mood; ishituh — of the Sovereign; abhut — arose; avalokya — seeing (it); nemuh — bowed; ardra-nayanah — with moist eyes; jagat-isham — to the Lord of the world; tushtuvuh — praised; cha — and; muditah — joyful; dvija-varyah — the best of the twice-born.

22And at once the mood of the Sovereign arose once more in Bhagavan. Seeing this, the best of the twice-born bowed with tear-filled eyes to the Lord of the world and joyfully praised Him.

Verse 23

एवं निनाय भगवान्सकलां निशां स
प्रातर्जगाम निजमन्दिरमिन्दुवक्त्रः।
हस्तगृहीतवरदण्ड इवातिचण्ड-
रश्मेः शिखेव नृहरिर्ददृशे जनेन॥२३॥

evaṁ nināya bhagavānsakalāṁ niśāṁ sa
prātarjagāma nijamandiraminduvaktraḥ|
hastagṛhītavaradaṇḍa ivāticaṇḍa-
raśmeḥ śikheva nṛharirdadṛśe janena||23||

evam — thus; ninaya — spent; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sakalam — the whole; nisham — night; sah — He; pratah — in the morning; jagama — went; nija-mandiram — to His house; indu-vaktrah — moon-faced; hasta-grihita-vara-dandah — holding a fine staff in His hand; iva — as if; ati-chanda-rashmeh — of the fierce-rayed sun; shikha — a flame; iva — like; nriharih — Nrihari; dadrishe — was seen; janena — by the people.

23Thus Bhagavan spent the whole night, and in the morning the moon-faced Lord went to His house; as though holding a splendid staff in His hand, Nrihari appeared to the people like a flame of the fierce-rayed sun.

Thus ends the sixteenth sarga, "The Manifestation of All Energies" (Sarva-shakti-prakasha), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The play in Chandrashekhara's house (see sarga 2.15) continues: Haridasa comes out first, staff in hand, like a herald or a watchman.
  2. Advaita is called a "portion" (kala) of the Lord, as in 1.04.5; this does not diminish Him: according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching He is Maha-Vishnu Himself (together with Sadashiva), non-different from the Lord.
  3. Baladeva is Nityananda.
  4. Vasudeva is a name of Krishna. The compound may also be understood as "in a special attire prepared by Vasudeva."
  5. The breeze from the Malaya hills in South India, where sandalwood grows, is famed in poetry for its coolness and fragrance.
  6. Kamala is Lakshmi, the Lord's eternal consort.
  7. The Goddess (Bhagavati) is the original energy of the Lord, possessing all powers. The energy is non-different from the Possessor of energy; that is why the Lord displays her mood here, and then once more the mood of the Sovereign (v. 22).
  8. Chandi is the fierce Goddess (Durga). The Lord jokes: people will take those devoted to Him in the form of the Goddess for Shaktas, votaries of Chandi.
